newsitem.title: CHINA: China to launch 30 satellites within century.
newsitem.headline: China to launch 30 satellites within century.

text.p: China is to use its Long March rockets to launch 30 satellites for other countries within the century, the Xinhua Daily Telegraph said on Wednesday.
A telecommunications satellite co-produced by China and Brazil would be launched soon, Wang Liheng, vice-president of the Aviation Industries of China, was quoted as saying.
Work on the satellite for transmitting commercial network data, a joint venture involving China, Germany and France, was near completion, Wang said. He gave no further details on the planned launch.
China has carried out 43 launches using Long March rockets with a success rate of 87 percent, he said. There are eight models of Long March rockets.
Wang said China has successfully launched 48 man-made satellites -- 38 made in China and 10 international commercial satellites.

The 10 international satellites included Asiasat-1, Asiasat-2, Asia-Pacific 1, Apstar 2, Echostar 1, two Australian telecommunication satellites and a piggy-back service on an experimental scientific satellite for Pakistan, Wang said.

The Chinese aviation and aerospace industry has built a complete system for research, design, production and experimental use of satellites, Wang said, adding that Long March rockets have attained a high technological level.
China's space industry, once much admired for its bargain prices and record of launch successes, has been plagued by problems in recent years.
In August, a domestic communications satellite launched aboard a Long March 3 rocket from Xichang in Sichuan province failed to reach its proper orbit.
In February, a Long March 3B carrying an Intel satellite veered wildly seconds after lift-off, before exploding in mid-air near the Xichang space centre.

China said six people were killed, 57 injured and 80 homes destroyed in that incident. Video footage smuggled out of China by an Israeli scientist showed dozens of levelled buildings and suggested the casualties were higher.
In January 1995, a Long March 2E rocket blew up, killing a family of six in a rain of debris and destroying the Apstar 2 satellite it was carrying.
